subject: Preserve short-lived data for active incident response
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@finpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+oncall@finpay.com, finpay-security@finpay.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: High-severity: request to preserve token-level traces for debugging

Hi Monica,

We’re in the middle of a high-severity production incident affecting payment authorizations (error 502 spikes since 08:30 PDT). Our on-call team captured a set of traces and a KV dump that point to a model routing mismatch. Support asked us to request a short, preserved window of request/response payloads and KV cache snapshots from the Redwood side so we can reproduce the race locally.

Can you preserve the last 72 hours of request logs and the per-request token traces for the affected environment (finpay-prod-us-west) while we triage? We understand retention policies, so we’re asking for a timebox and strict access controls — only FinPay ops and FinPay security will access the bundle. We can provide an access checklist and will delete the snapshot asap when the incident is closed.

I attached an error bundle (error_dump_20260812.tar.gz) and included the incident JIRA (INC-9813). Please let me know the earliest you can confirm preservation and who from Redwood will be on the topology call.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Sr. Reliability Engineer, FinPay

Attachments: error_dump_20260812.tar.gz (log bundle)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: High-severity: request to preserve token-level traces for debugging

Folks — forwarding FinPay’s ask. Short summary: payment auth errors, asking us to preserve request/response payloads + token traces and KV cache snapshots for finpay-prod-us-west for triage. They propose a 72-hour window and limited access.

Questions I have before we approve the window:
- Exact scope: full request bodies vs. filtered PII? FinPay says only FinPay ops will access, but we need to redact any customer PII prior to handing off.
- Access model: will this be a sealed bundle we deliver to FinPay’s S3 or do they require our engineers to run a temporary retrieval session?
- Audit: we need a signed SLA exemption form (attached draft) and a JIRA link for the preservation action.

Can Rishi confirm security constraints and Naomi confirm commercial/contract implications (SLA carveouts)? I’m happy to approve a short, timeboxed preservation if we get explicit answers and a signed form.

Monica Patel
Senior Support Engineer — Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded message ---
On Wed, 12 Aug 2026 at 09:14 Sara Liu <sara.liu@finpay.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High-severity: request to preserve token-level traces for debugging

Thanks for the ping. Security can approve a tightly-scoped, time-limited preservation under the following conditions:
- Scope limited to requests that match the FinPay incident timeframe and service (finpay-prod-us-west) — no broad account-wide retention.
- All PII must be redacted before any external transfer; if redaction cannot be guaranteed we will provide a sealed access session where FinPay engineers can connect to the snapshot from their IP allowlist under supervision.
- Access will be logged to our audit backend and keys rotated immediately after retrieval.
- Maximum preservation window: 48 hours from the time we snapshot.

Please confirm FinPay agrees to those constraints. If they accept, Security will prepare an exemption ticket and provide the minimal ACLs required. I’ll need the list of FinPay users (email addresses) who require access.

— Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

> On Wed, 12 Aug 2026 at 09:31 Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > (forwarded message quoted)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: High-severity: request to preserve token-level traces for debugging

Monica / team —

I’m okay to move forward with a 48-hour preservation window under the security conditions Rishi listed. Operational notes:
- Naomi, please confirm whether we need an SLA carveout signed by FinPay legal for this one-off preservation or whether the existing contract covers emergency access for debugging. If legal needs it, Naomi, please create the draft and loop Legal.
- Monica, please produce a narrow snapshot (by service id + time-window) and flag any artifacts that contain full request bodies. Prefer providing a sealed retrieval session rather than pushing raw logs to an external bucket unless redaction is confirmed.
- Rishi, once the exemption ticket is created, please add tracers to the audit record and set the ACL to the FinPay emails Sara provided.

Monica — please confirm with FinPay that 48 hours is acceptable and ask for a short list of FinPay users who need access. Also attach the SLA exemption form I’ve started (sla_exemption_form.pdf).

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
